req.title: Register rejects duplicate username
req.statement: The system shall render an error message when POST /auth/register is called with a username already present in the users table.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that POST /auth/register must render an error message when a duplicate username is submitted. The pre-loaded database already contains users Rahul, Anjali, Ishaan, Diya, and James. Tests cover: (1) positive — a genuinely new username registers successfully and redirects to /auth/login; (2) negative — submitting an existing username returns HTTP 200 with the exact error string 'User <name> is already registered.'; (3) boundary — registering the same username twice in sequence within one test session (first succeeds, second fails), exercising the state transition from 'not registered' to 'registered'; (4) additional negative — each pre-loaded username triggers the exact error message, verifying the constant string; (5) boundary — a username that differs by one character from an existing one is accepted, catching off-by-one or substring mutations in the duplicate check.

tests.name: test_register_new_user_succeeds
preconditions: Database is initialised with pre-loaded rows
Username 'Newuser' does not exist in the users table
trace: R-FLASKR-006 — happy path: unique username must be accepted
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()
r = client.post('/auth/register', data={'username': 'Newuser', 'password': 'pass123'})
assert r.status_code == 302
assert r.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login'
assert b'already registered' not in r.data

def test_register_new_user_succeeds():
    fd2, path2 = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd2)
    app2 = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path2})
    with app2.app_context():
        init_db()
    c = app2.test_client()
    resp = c.post('/auth/register', data={'username': 'Newuser', 'password': 'pass123'})
    assert resp.status_code == 302
    assert resp.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login'
    assert b'already registered' not in resp.data

tests.name: test_register_all_preloaded_usernames_are_duplicates
preconditions: Database is initialised with pre-loaded rows containing Rahul, Anjali, Ishaan, Diya, James
actions: POST /auth/register for each pre-loaded username with a fresh password
expected: Each response body contains 'User <name> is already registered.' with the exact username
trace: R-FLASKR-006 — decision table: every pre-loaded username triggers the duplicate error
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

def test_register_all_preloaded_usernames_are_duplicates():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    preloaded = ['Rahul', 'Anjali', 'Ishaan', 'Diya', 'James']
    for name in preloaded:
        r = client.post('/auth/register', data={'username': name, 'password': 'testpass'})
        assert r.status_code == 200, f'Expected 200 for duplicate {name}, got {r.status_code}'
        expected_msg = f'User {name} is already registered.'.encode()
        assert expected_msg in r.data, f'Error message not found for {name}'

Response body does NOT contain a redirect or success indicator

import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

def test_register_duplicate_error_message_exact_format():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.post('/auth/register', data={'username': 'James', 'password': 'newpass'})
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert b'User James is already registered.' in r.data
    assert b'User james is already registered.' not in r.data
    assert b'james' not in r.data or b'James' in r.data
    assert r.headers.get('Location') is None
